To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the tracer influx parameter Ki was found to be significantly higher in tumors compared to healthy prostate tissue; (2) the tracer influx parameters were higher in high grade tumors than in low grade tumors; (3) the effect of scan duration on Ki was minimal for scans lasting 10-20 min; (4) the tracer influx rate constant Ki was found to have a higher correlation with Gleason score than SUV.
the kinetic analysis of choline PET imaging is able to differentiate between tumor grades and that the kinetic exchange rate constant, k2, can be used as a biomarker for disease staging.
18F-florocholine uptake is correlated to histological tumor grade in prostate cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantification of 18F-florocholine uptake in prostate cancer using PET and the relationship between tracer uptake and disease stage and grade.
the quantification of 18F-florocholine in prostate cancer and the relationship between kinetic parameters and histological grade.
the quantification and analysis of 18F-fludrocholine uptake in prostate cancer and its correlation with histological tumor grade.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the tracer influx parameters are the best for the evaluation of prostate cancer, but they are not always the best for the comparison of uptake values between different subjects, and the use of Patlak analysis is recommended.
the kinetic parameters of 18F-CH uptake in prostate cancer tissue are not significantly affected by the histology grade.

the use of 18F-choline PET for prostate cancer imaging is a valuable tool for the detection of primary tumors and metastatic disease, with the caveat that the tracer is not a specific marker for prostate cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kinetic analysis of choline uptake in prostate tumors provides a more accurate and robust measure of tracer uptake than Patlak and SUV analyses.
18F-FC uptake is not a good indicator of prostate tumor aggressiveness.

the tracer influx rate constants from full compartmental modeling are the most robust kinetic parameters for quantifying tracer uptake in the prostate and that these parameters are highly correlated with Gleason score, which is an important prognostic factor for prostate cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tracer influx rate constant Ki can be used as a robust and accurate measure of tumor uptake.
18F-florocholine PET can be used to differentiate between benign and malignant prostate tissue.
the kinetic exchange rate constant, k2, is the parameter that best correlates with Gleason score.
